thesis:
One sentence holds the whole file together: at a ~5% risk-free rate with $365tn of global debt, capital stops paying for narrative and starts paying for chokepoints. Every recurring observation across six weeks of briefs points the same direction — electrons, molecules, memory bits, fab capacity, transmission, fuel cycle, payment/exchange rails and now the agent identity-and-containment layer. The AI story has quietly stopped being a story about models and become a story about power procurement and governance plumbing: Google signing a 20-year nuclear PPA with Constellation, Meta funding seven gas plants, Amazon's $8bn Generac order, Mitsui buying LNG explicitly for data centers, Korea's reported $200bn into US nuclear/LNG/gas. When an advertising company signs a two-decade PPA, the scarce input has been identified and it is not silicon. The second-order read is that the AI drawdown, when it comes, will be a financing event (vendor equity, insurer-wrapped GPU loans, circular hyperscaler commitments), not a demand event — which means the physical assets keep their cash flows while the levered intermediaries do not.

On the human side, the dominant substitution of this decade is security replacing convenience as the premium good, and time replacing intelligence as what people actually buy from AI. Households are purchasing reliability (onsite generation, fixed tariffs, grid-failure searches), institutions are purchasing containment (identity, audit, kill switches for agents), and states are purchasing sovereignty (fuel cycle, fabs, rare earths, tungsten stockpiles). Simultaneously, consumers buy agents to reclaim hours — 'ai phone assistant', 'ai phone answering service', ~1bn monthly mobile assistant users — which is a time purchase, not a knowledge purchase, and it reallocates attention away from ad-funded surfaces toward agent surfaces. That is the largest re-plumbing of consumer economics since mobile, and it is why advertising attention platforms are both the incumbent and the thing being disintermediated.

The third durable line is adaptation rather than resolution in housing and mobility. At 7%+ mortgages households do not become distressed, they become frozen: historic-low layoffs with near-zero hiring, no moves, no refis, duration-stretched car loans. The behavioural output is remodel-over-relocate, rent-over-own, multigenerational and smaller formats, and institutional rental permanence. Housing undersupply does not clear; it is financed away from, with capital explicitly rotating out of dwellings into data centers (Kashkari's framing). That makes maintenance/MRO, rental operators and renovation retail the durable trade rather than homebuilding volume — and the attention data (HD, LOW spiking while flagged not-priced) says the market has not marked this behavioural substitution. Underneath everything, demography (Western populations shrinking from ~2029) and debt service exceeding nominal GDP growth make productivity-per-worker — automation, agents, healthspan — the only growth lever and permanent term premium the discount rate everyone must underwrite against.

For capital: own the constraint and the toll booth, rent nothing whose moat was cheap capital. Generation, grid EPC, fuel cycle, memory, optics, security-as-metered-utility, exchanges and brokers are the compounding claims. Pure compute landlords, seat-priced software, mass premium apparel, card-network toll economics and marginal housing are the structurally contested ones.

theme_ranking.why: The single most repeated, most corroborated shift in the file: a 20-year nuclear PPA signed by an ad company, Meta funding seven gas plants, ERCOT 2030s demand, Duke raising 2026 guidance. Generation has pricing power it has not had in forty years and the demand is contracted, not forecast.

Electricity availability, not GPU supply, is the binding constraint. Transmission EPC, switchgear, turbines, behind-the-meter generation and demand flexibility are a decade-long capex channel with a skilled-labour bottleneck protecting contractor margins.

Converts from defensive cost centre to metered utility on every agent action — identity, delegation, containment, audit. Tops all flow rankings, non-discretionary budget, and regulation (state-by-state AI employment law) will eventually mandate what Nvidia's reference architecture already defines.

Italy reversing a 40-year ban, Poland's mega-project, Korea's $200bn, Singapore studying it, uranium at a record high while equities lag. Sovereign capital allocation, not a commodity cycle — the dislocation resolves in favour of the fuel cycle and merchant generators.

Demand is real and self-funding at hyperscaler level, but the financing is circular (vendor equity, insurer-wrapped GPU loans). Own the memory, optics and power-adjacent layers; be skeptical of pure compute landlords whose terminal value is contestable by edge inference.

Memory is the tightest link and least exposed to a frontier-model pause because inference and edge consume HBM/DRAM regardless of training cadence. Sovereignty spending (Sanand, Australia) adds a policy floor; offset by China TAM going structurally to zero.

Unbundling across time, access and venue simultaneously — tokenized equities, weekend trading, TXSE at $100bn listings, retail private-market access. Rails, venues and brokers capture the share shift; asset gatherers pay for it. Also the vehicle for the retirement-advice demographic wave.

Gas is the marginal AI fuel over three years and LNG is being contracted explicitly for data centers (Mitsui). Hormuz episodes and diesel export-ban proposals show energy security is now a geopolitical instrument, structurally short-listing US shale and LNG operators.

Moving from budget headlines to contracted backlog (Anduril $2.9bn), with infrastructure now a wartime target and stockpiling (tungsten, rare earths) becoming policy. Explicitly flagged 'not priced' in the attention data — rare combination of backlog visibility and unpriced attention.

Agents are bought as time, and ~1bn monthly mobile users proves the behaviour. But value accrues to distribution incumbents and to the governance layer, not to seat-priced software (Adobe, Wix) or standalone model vendors — so conviction in the theme exceeds conviction in most of its pure-plays.

Supply-chain sovereignty is the long war, not tariffs. Multi-decade allocated spend on fabs, materials processing and domestic production, which raises the structural cost base and keeps goods inflation stickier than 2010-2019 — even when industrial flows read negative today.

A 107% surge in robotic-surgery intent with granular procedure-level queries, plus Medtronic raising guidance, and the dataset explicitly flags it as unpriced. Aging demographics buying restored function is one of the most reliable demand curves available.

Cost, latency and privacy push inference onto devices; attention at 82 with surging assistant queries. This is simultaneously the best long-term silicon demand story and the main structural risk to centralized compute-rental economics.
Grid, data centre and electrification demand collide with constrained supply. High physical conviction, but the timing is macro-dependent — it reprices after the growth scare passes, not during it.

$365tn debt, 30-year near 6%, inflation framed by policy as the debt-rebalancing mechanism, and measurement methodology itself becoming untrustworthy. Caveat: the briefs repeatedly observe investors currently satisfying the store-of-value need with yield rather than metal — right thesis, wrong current flow.

Demography (shrinking Western populations from ~2029) makes labour substitution structurally necessary, and humanoids have entered consumer imagination. But the market now demands unit economics and construction robotics explicitly does not solve housing this cycle — real, slow, over-narrated near term.

$250k/yr longevity care establishes a premium tier that trickles into diagnostics and early detection (Grail +180%). Durable demographic need; monetization path still unproven outside the top income decile.

Azure at 43% shows the monetization layer still wins and cloud/AI credentials are repricing the labour market (+53% salary/certification queries). But investors now pay for cash conversion and punish capex — the theme compounds, the multiple does not.

The undersupply is real and does not resolve, but it is financed away from at 5%. The investable expression is rental, remodel, MRO and multigenerational formats — not homebuilder volumes, which face price cuts, political backlash and capital rotating into data centers.

Trading down is the most consistently observed consumer behaviour in the file (Walmart, TJX, dollar stores vs Nike's worst year ever), funded increasingly by credit in the bottom two quintiles. Durable but widely recognised and low-margin.

Tokenized equities at 11% of DEX volume, SEC approval, stablecoin attention +64%, favourable policy drift (FinCEN, PAC money). The rails thesis is credible; the asset-price thesis is not what the evidence supports.

Starship reaching orbit compresses mass-to-orbit cost and Google is siting data centers in orbit — genuine pull-forward of constellation, defense and in-space compute. Still early, capital-hungry, and dependent on a single launch provider's cadence.

Robotaxi programmes and autonomous freight (Einride) are scaling, and truck-ownership economics are breaking at record diesel. But Tesla Semi's flat reception shows the market is now unit-economics-first; revenue recognition lags the narrative by years.

Normalised and increasingly a share war (Lilly gaining, Novo rebranding/'rethinking') with payer pressure and deteriorating sector flows. The need is permanent; the pricing power is visibly eroding — this is a volume story now, not a margin story.

Spending volumes hold up, but the evidence points at the toll economics being structurally threatened by stablecoin rails and Asian payment systems over a decade, and Visa is already cutting headcount. Hold the rails, not the take rate.

Bifurcated: Carnival's record deposits and loyalty tiers against Ryanair cutting winter capacity, Southwest's fuel squeeze and NCLH near lows. People still want the experience; at $100+ oil the operator often cannot sell it profitably. Status-dense premium wins, mid-tier loses.

The attention pool is migrating to short-form commerce, live rights and agent surfaces. Incumbents hold the intent today, but agents that do things rather than show things are the largest threat to ad economics since mobile — the theme is structurally contested, not structurally growing.

Delivery aggregation substitutes for personal trips as car ownership costs bite, but a distillate squeeze taxes last-mile directly and the agent-shopping standoff threatens who owns the transaction. Volumes grow, margins get fought over.

Real and durable — more US cards pay for streaming than cinema and concerts combined — but it is a finished reallocation, now a mature, competitive, content-cost-inflating business. Low incremental alpha from a known fact.

beneficiary_profiles: Constraint owners: merchant generators, nuclear fleets, uranium/fuel-cycle, pipeline and LNG infrastructure — the scarce input in the AI buildout, with 20-year contracted cash flows from investment-grade hyperscaler counterparties.

Picks-and-shovels for electrons: grid EPC and transmission contractors, switchgear and turbine OEMs, behind-the-meter generation and mechanical/electrical specialty contractors protected by a skilled-trades labour bottleneck.
Metered toll roads on agent actions: identity, delegation, containment, audit and per-action security — non-discretionary budget lines that scale with AI deployment volume rather than model quality.

Bit-level chokepoints: HBM/DRAM, advanced packaging, optics and fiber — consumption scales with inference and edge deployment regardless of training cadence, insulating them from a frontier-model pause.
Venue and rail owners: exchanges, brokers, custody and tokenization rails that monetize transaction volume, 24/7 access and new listing venues irrespective of whether underlying asset prices rise.
Maintenance and in-place-upgrade economics: MRO, home improvement retail, rental operators and renovation supply — beneficiaries of frozen housing turnover rather than of housing recovery.

Restored-function healthcare: robotic surgery platforms with razor-and-blade annuities, cardiac and orthopedic devices, continuous monitoring and early-detection diagnostics serving an aging, procedure-shopping population.
Policy-mandated resilience: defense primes with contracted backlog, grid hardening, stockpiled critical materials and domestic processing — demand set by statute and threat, not by the cycle.
Cash-generative short-duration compounders with pricing power: the only valuation profile that survives a permanently elevated term premium.
Trading-down retail with scale buying power: off-price and value formats capturing wallet share from mass premium brands in a credit-funded bottom-half consumer.

anti_theses: 'AI is a GPU shortage story.' The evidence says electricity, siting and interconnection are binding, not silicon. Compute landlords and second-tier AI capex are the contested layer; generation and memory are the scarce ones.

'China AI revenue is recovery optionality for Western accelerator vendors.' Huawei's Ascend 960 on a Q1 2027 timetable means China share of Western AI semiconductor TAM should be modelled toward zero, not as a call option.

'Rates revert to 3% and housing unfreezes.' $365tn of global debt, a 30-year near 6%, debt service above nominal GDP growth and shrinking Western populations from 2029 make elevated term premium the regime. Underwrite homebuilder volumes against 5%, not against a reversion.

'The housing shortage gets solved by construction robotics or by building more.' Humanoid homebuilders are years away and builders are cutting price rather than volume. The shortage is adapted to — rental, remodel, multigenerational, smaller formats — not resolved.

'Gold is the obvious hedge right now.' The briefs repeatedly observe the opposite behaviour: gold at seven-week lows while 19-year-high Treasury yields absorb the store-of-value demand. The need is being met by income, not metal, as long as real rates rise.

'GLP-1s are a durable pricing-power franchise.' The file shows a share war, Novo 'rethinking' strategy, payer pressure and deteriorating sector flows. It is becoming a volume and distribution business, and it raises the burden of proof on CGM and continuous-monitoring franchises to show incremental value.

'Seat-priced software captures the AI productivity gain.' Adobe's soft guidance and Wix's cut are the tell. Enterprises pay for measurable labour substitution and for per-agent identity and liability — not for more seats.

'Advertising platforms are the natural owners of the AI consumer.' Agents that do things rather than show things disintermediate the ad surface. Owning intent is contested (Meta vs Amazon standoff), and the incumbent position is a defence, not a growth thesis.

'An AI unwind would prove demand was fake.' The circularity is in the financing — vendor equity stakes, insurer-wrapped GPU loans, vendor-linked cloud commitments. The drawdown, when it comes, hits capital structures; contracted power and memory consumption keep running.

'Consumer spending resilience signals household health.' Spending is being funded from paper wealth and credit — confidence at a 12-year low, 9.3m student-loan defaults, Great-Recession-level card delinquency in parts of the country, investments tapped for consumption. The income base is being optimized away even as spend holds.
what_would_change: A sustained fall in the 10-year below ~3.5% with mortgage rates following: that would unfreeze housing turnover, revive levered and long-duration business models, and invalidate the 'cheap capital moat is impaired' spine of the thesis.

Evidence that inference costs collapse faster than demand grows — so that total electricity demand from AI plateaus. That would break the power-compute convergence, the most heavily weighted conviction here.

Local political resistance to data-center siting (water, tariffs on household bills, 'ai data center near me' queries) escalating into binding moratoria in Texas, Virginia or the Midwest — which would redirect the buildout offshore or into orbit and re-rate domestic generation assets downward.

Hyperscaler capex guidance actually being cut, not just punished by investors: a financing event at a neocloud, insurer withdrawal from GPU loan wraps, or a failed vendor-financed deal cascading into order cancellations.

Statutory federal AI safety regulation that mandates a government standard rather than ratifying a private reference architecture — that would commoditize the agent-governance annuity instead of concentrating it.

A durable energy price collapse (OPEC+ capacity returning, Hormuz de-escalation holding, crude back under $60) which would relieve the household budget squeeze, revive mid-tier experiences and travel, and weaken the energy-security-as-consumer-need shift.

Robotic surgery and continuous-monitoring attention fading back to baseline without procedure volume or device revenue following — that would reclassify the 107% query surge as a headline rather than a demand curve.
Stablecoin or tokenized-rail volumes showing actual revenue impact on card networks, which would accelerate the digital-payments de-rating from a decade-out hypothesis to a live thesis.

A genuine labour-market break — layoffs rising from historic lows rather than hiring staying at 29k — which would convert 'frozen households' into 'distressed households' and shift the trade from value retail and remodel toward outright defensives and duration.

Humanoid or construction robotics demonstrating unit economics at scale (verified cost-per-task below loaded labour) within two years rather than five — that would move robotics-automation from mid-table to top-five conviction.
